chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Player pianos and phonographs in Harlem summers
summary: In summer he heard piano rolls and Jelly Roll Morton disks from open windows.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, we've gone right back now. So let's go through the piano players.

So therefore, all the things that I was exposed to in my early childhood, I don't see why I didn't... You know, I should have really made more of that. Because later on I heard... I came to see Clarence Profit. And usually in the summertime, all the houses were open, the windows were open, and there was a conglomeration of piano rolls and player pianos being played! And in the summertime you would hear "Sweet Georgia Brown" and things coming from various apartment houses in the street. It was, you know, 120th Street...
I think somebody told me that Lucky Roberts, though, had pianos in about two or three rooms of his apartment.

Well, this was back when I don't think he... I didn't know he was... He was Mr. Roberts at that time! I'm not speaking about the years later, after I knew, you know... He became Lucky Roberts in my manhood. I'm not talking about...

Exactly. And then, of course, "Ain't Misbehaving" came out, and... Anyway, people had these large Victrolas, and you could hear the Jelly Roll Morton disks being played, you know. It was orthophonic! And that's
what... Hey, that became... you know, it was my stimulation, I mean, to hear these Jazz pianists around...you know, Jazz itself.
